To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current regulatory system is ineffective in controlling pharmaceutical expenditures and is not in accordance with the constitutional principle of "legally".
the current pricing regulations are not only ineffective, but also unconstitutional, since they violate the principles of proportionality and legality.

(a) the Greek pharmaceutical market is characterized by a high level of pharmaceutical expenditure, (b) this is due to the high level of consumption of pharmaceutical products, (c) the main reason for the latter is that prices of pharmaceutical products are kept at a very low level and, (d) the main cause of the latter is the intervention of the state in the pharmaceutical market.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to regulate the Greek pharmaceutical market in a way that will be economically viable and legally defensible.

the following: (i) the economic and political characteristics of the Greek market, (ii) the legal and institutional structure of pharmaceutical regulation and (iii) the constitutional implications of pharmaceutical regulation.

the following: a) the impact of current pharmaceutical regulations on the pharmaceutical market, and the effect thereof on the financial stability of the social security system and the private sector; b) the political and legal aspects of current pricing regulations and their effect on pharmaceutical expenditure; c) the impact of European harmonisation of the pharmaceutical market on the Greek pharmaceutical market; d) an alternative regulatory paradigm for the pharmaceutical market, based on the experience of European Union member countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pharmaceutical policy of Greece is in a state of crisis, which can be resolved only if the state intervenes with a comprehensive and integrated regulatory policy.
pharmaceutical policy should be directed towards an efficient allocation of resources, which is to be achieved by a combination of price and volume controls.
the Greek pharmaceutical market is at a crossroad of change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Greek system of pharmaceutical regulation has been largely ineffective, as a result of the "unconstitutionality of its regulatory instruments.

pharmaceutical expenditure in Greece is largely affected by a paradox: the state's intervention is mainly directed to the rationalisation of total expenditure through pricing regulations, but all measures taken to-date are directed towards exhaustive price controls, i.e., interventions on the supply-side alone.

the Greek pharmaceutical market needs a new regulatory paradigm, which will be based on a new regulatory framework, that will be in line with the new European regulatory environment, and that will be founded on the principles of "legality" and "proportionality", as defined by the Greek constitution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a regulatory framework for pharmaceutical markets should be founded on a combination of economic and political considerations.

the Greek regulatory framework for pharmaceuticals is in dire need of a comprehensive reform, which should take place in the form of a legislative initiative that is in line with the constitutional principle of legality.

a comprehensive reform of the pharmaceutical market should be based on a combination of demand and supply side interventions, which should be implemented in the framework of an integrated pharmaceutical policy.
